requirements.text: log a new incident on her behalf ... high impact on the workforce ... high urgency
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_004' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND status = 'new'
requirements.source: Verify if the incident is created correctly.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023)
Aisha Williams is USER_004 (aisha.williams@techcorp.com, active, ORG_001), the only user of that name in the seed
priority follows the policy 3.1 matrix: impact high x urgency high = critical
status = new is the policy 3.1 default for every new incident; the original check does not test it
short_description is mandatory (policy 3.1) but free text, so it is not a cell

requirements.text: send her a notification requesting a scanned copy of her identity proof
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND email = 'aisha.williams@techcorp.com'
requirements.source: Verify if the notification is sent correctly.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007)
'her' is the caller USER_004, so the notification goes to aisha.williams@techcorp.com; 'this incident' is the incident created above, INC_024

type is not a cell: the request names none, the policy lists no notification types, the schema puts no constraint on the column, and the two benchmark copies disagree (other vs reminder); see original_checks
the message text (a scanned copy of her identity proof) is free text and not tested

disagreement: source: A carried the benchmark check repaired (type dropped), B excluded both copies and wrote this as new; the repaired form is kept because the check is right in every cell but the undecidable type, so carrying it keeps the benchmark's verdict linked to this requirement

requirements.text: link relevant knowledge article to this incident having password or authentication related details
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_kb_id = 'IKB_006' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_001' AND used_as = 'suggested'
requirements.source: Verify if the knowledge article is added.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_006 after IKB_005)
KB_001 'Password Reset Procedure' is the only published article in the incident's org ORG_001 about passwords or authentication
used_as = suggested per policy 7: articles matched at incident creation are linked as suggested

requirements.text: link relevant knowledge article to this incident having password or authentication related details
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND knowledge_id IN ('KB_004', 'KB_005')
assumptions: selector boundary: KB_004 (Email Account Recovery Steps) and KB_005 (Corporate Email Access Guide) mention locked accounts and authentication failures in their bodies but belong to ORG_002, outside the caller's org and the request's single 'article'

Verify if the notification is sent corre.evidence: the request and policy fix no notification type, the schema puts no constraint on the column, the seed never uses 'other', and the (2) copy says reminder instead; the type cell is undecidable and dropped, and the rest (NOTIF_008, INC_024, aisha.williams@techcorp.com) is carried

Verify if the incident is created correc.evidence: its priority = high contradicts the policy 3.1 matrix, where impact high x urgency high = critical; the first copy is the one kept

notes:
Merged from two independent passes that agree on every requirement's table, anchor, cells and SQL and on every value. disagreement: disposition of 'Verify if the notification is sent correctly.': A repaired (type cell dropped, check carried as source), B excluded both copies as undecidable and wrote a new requirement for the common core; the repaired form is kept because the check is right in every cell but the undecidable type, so the requirement keeps the benchmark's name as source and the (2) copy is excluded as its duplicate. disagreement: form: the KB_004/KB_005 stay has empty cells in A and the knowledge_id predicate in B; B's form is kept. Acting user USER_001 is an active admin, so logging on another user's behalf is within scope. The incident's org_id, short_description, category, channel and assignment are not tested: the request fixes none of them and this policy (4afd943b) gives no default for any. Policy 3.1 lists opened_by as a mandatory input, but the incident table has no such column, so nothing is tested for it. The notification type was the hardest call for both passes: the benchmark's two copies disagree (other vs reminder), the policy has no notification enumeration, and the seed's types (alert, reminder, update, solution_proposal, report) do not settle it, so the type is left untested rather than picking one.
revised: the KB_004/KB_005 stay's cells are now empty: its selector already fixes knowledge_id IN ('KB_004', 'KB_005'), so repeating that predicate in cells restated the selector; its sql and count are unchanged.
revised: the reason for carrying the notification check repaired now stands on its own (every cell but the undecidable type is right, so the benchmark's verdict stays linked to the requirement), in the notification requirement's assumptions and in the disposition disagreement above.
